why: permitted only when every record comes from the same host and the same series shape; otherwise the ratio mixes engines with hardware and is the confound this study exists to avoid
reading_guide: mongo-default is MongoDB as a team would deploy it: nothing indexed that was not asked for. mongo-wildcard is MongoDB doing HCD's job: every field queryable without declaration. Quoting the first against HCD overstates MongoDB's advantage; quoting only the second understates how MongoDB is actually used. Report both or report neither.

VERDICT.who_costs_more: HCD, decisively, on the single-field-mutation axis.
VERDICT.by_how_much: per indexed KiB: HCD 0.7775 ms vs mongo-wildcard 0.0176 ms (44x) and mongo-default 0.0098 ms (79x). Absolute update p50: HCD 41-131 ms rising with size; MongoDB ~5.5-7.6 ms, essentially flat.
VERDICT.why: MongoDB $set mutates the targeted field without rewriting the document and maintains only declared indexes; even with a wildcard index (HCD's job), its per-byte mutation cost stays near zero. HCD reads, rewrites the whole document plus eleven derived columns, maintains nine SAI, and guards with a Paxos round — all growing with indexed bytes.
VERDICT.durability_matched: MongoDB w:majority+j:true (2-of-3) vs HCD LOCAL_QUORUM+LOCAL_SERIAL (2-of-3); the mapping is a declared judgement. The Paxos-vs-document-atomicity asymmetry is a design difference, not aligned.
VERDICT.expected_direction: This is the result the article's own reasoning predicts; MongoDB's documented in-place update is structurally cheaper on this axis.
